Build your own

Choose the enclosure that fits.

Every option protects the Arduino UNO Q and keeps its Matrix visible. The difference is where the Arduino USB-C hub lives and which cables need direct access.

UNO Q Case

The smallest design. The hub stays outside the enclosure and connects through the UNO Q USB-C opening.

Download its print files

Controller Dock V1

The original low-profile dock keeps the hub visible in an open rear service bay for a fixed cable layout.

Download its print files

Controller Dock V2

The hub is fully enclosed, with rear USB-C access, internal USB-A routing, and optional side Ethernet access.

Download its print files

Hardware

  • Arduino UNO Q
  • UVC USB camera
  • Arduino USB-C Hub (8 in 1) and suitable power supply
  • Physical controller already supported by the selected console
  • Fasteners, heat-set inserts, rubber feet, and the printed enclosure

Before you print

Print the fit coupons first. Choose one structural base, one matching lid, and one matching branding set. The large target badge is an optional decoration and does not fit a lid recess.

The starting profile targets an Anycubic Kobra 3, PLA, a 0.4 mm nozzle, and 0.20 mm layers. Other printers can use the same geometry after checking clearances.
